title: How Vercel's v0 reached 3,200 merged PRs a day by bringing git workflow to vibe coding
summary: Guillermo Rauch demos v0's new git-native workflow (branches, previews, PRs) using skills.sh. He argues vibe coding is easy at zero-to-one but hard at scale, and that production rigor lets non-engineers ship, collapsing prioritization friction.

principles.text: Vibe coding's real test is iterating and deploying safely at scale, not the zero-to-one demo.
principles.quote: It's really easy to go from zero to one. Like I think we've all seen the demos of I prom thing and it's cool and I think what's harder is to iterate on a project at scale and to deploy changes safely.

principles.text: Give AI-built changes real engineering process: branches, previews, code review, merge.
principles.quote: we always work on branches and we take advantage of branch previews and then we code review and then we merge them.

principles.text: Let non-engineers prototype and hand off as a PR, so ideas stop living in prototype land.
principles.quote: until I had this mechanism to hand it off as a pull request to the engineering team then I was kind of like playing in La La Lands.

principles.text: Lowering the friction to get something live shifts debate from prioritizing hypotheses to judging real ideas.
principles.quote: the humiliation ritual of prioritization goes away and you can actually focus your time on defending the merits of an idea

principles.text: Hold internal products to the same bar as external launches so you know people will adopt them.
principles.quote: when we cook on a on a project or a product internally, we hold ourselves to the same sort of high bar as if you had launched a product externally

principles.text: Use a 'customer zero' (yourselves) plus 'customer one' (close design partners) to validate what to build.
principles.quote: There's a customer zero and a customer one. Customer zero, we like to to be ourselves.
